root_cause_label: Build Abandonment After Correct Patch (No Distribution Rebuild)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly patched the directory traversal vulnerability in FileUploadHandler.java but aborted two consecutive Maven build attempts (steps 103, 105) because they were slow, then substituted standalone Java test scripts for the explicitly required distribution rebuild.
t_err_evidence: Step 103: Agent sends C-c to interrupt the Maven build (`mvn clean compile -pl flink-runtime -am -DskipTests`) citing it was 'taking a while', despite the task specification explicitly requiring a distribution rebuild after patching.
t_commit_evidence: Step 105: Agent sends a second C-c aborting a retry of the Maven build, after which it pivots permanently to standalone javac/java verification and never attempts another Maven build. The failing outcome is now locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 103: The Ctrl-C interrupt of the Maven build is the first observable signal that the required distribution rebuild will not be completed.
trigger_explanation: The task specification explicitly required rebuilding the Flink distribution (`mvn -DskipTests clean package -pl flink-dist -am`) after patching, and the acceptance criteria stated the project must build successfully. The agent started a Maven build at step 102 but interrupted it twice (steps 103, 105) because it was slow, treating this mandatory step as optional. The agent never returned to the build and instead used standalone Java compilation as a proxy for verification, unaware it was skipping a critical requirement.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 15-96: The str_replace editor tool repeatedly failed to match tab-indented code (steps 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 24, 26, 28, 30-36, 39-40, 52, 72, 80), forcing the agent to use backup/restore cycles and Python scripts to apply the patch. This tool friction consumed approximately 80 steps and likely contributed to the agent's impatience when the Maven build was slow.
